title: Unprefixed credential names reach the launched child verbatim (MODEL_API_KEY)
description: Found by the Fable-lane credential-boundary review of agentic-sdlc-71f4 and reproduced identically against HEAD, so it is pre-existing rather than a regression: the environment scrub denies ANTHROPIC_*/CLAUDE_*/AWS_* by prefix plus three named unprefixed hazards (NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED, FALLBACK_FOR_ALL_PRIMARY_MODELS, API_TIMEOUT_MS), so an unprefixed credential name is not swept. Measured: MODEL_API_KEY reaches the child verbatim alongside ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN carrying the same value. Decide whether the deny policy gains an unprefixed credential-name class (and how it stays maintainable without becoming a value scanner - ADR-0010 Amendment A deliberately makes this a NAME policy), or whether the limit is documented and accepted. Related documented limit from the same review: a secret an operator sets under an allowed name crosses as that variable value.

title: Record every wave node disposition in an append-only wave journal
description: Slice 5 substrate (issue 07 State/continuation + Completion conditions 1 and 7). One read/append tool owning the wave journal: each node records inputs, outputs, RuntimeAssignment, timestamps, result, and evidence, and every required node reaches exactly one of admitted success, approved skip, or explicit blocked disposition. Also records budgets, retries, plan revisions, and approvals so condition 7 traceability is derivable rather than asserted. Append-only with effect admission at the instant a record becomes durable (the effect-admission class rule); a partial append is exit 4, never a clean refusal. Deterministic canonical JSON, schema-tagged.

title: Admit or refuse a RuntimeAssignment before spawn and detect unexplained substitution
description: Slice 5 dispatch admission (issue 07 Roles/authority/routing + Completion condition 2; AGENTS.md RuntimeAssignment rules). Read-only admission tool: resolution_state must be resolved, exact model and effort request injection is mandatory and immutable, requested tier and resolved provider/model stay separate facts, resolved is recorded only after adapter readback, and requested/inherited/unresolved/incomplete stops before dispatch and therefore before spawn with a named refusal plus a SeedProposal shape. Separately: given a receipt, decide whether the served provider/model matches what was requested and classify any difference as explained substitution or UNEXPLAINED (which blocks wave completion). Effective effort/context readback may be honestly unavailable and requested values never become readback.

title: Derive the terminal wave verdict: accepted, remediation-progress, or blocked
description: Slice 5 EXIT ARTIFACT (map build-sequence step 5; product spec 597-603; issue 07 Completion and adversarial review). Compose the wave journal, RuntimeAssignment admissions, workstream review verdicts, fan-in authorization, the gate receipt and baseline comparison, and the critic findings into exactly one terminal state: accepted (normal delivery wave, authoritative repository gate passes, all eight completion conditions met), remediation-progress (focused gates pass AND the exact global failure baseline does not worsen; never claims gate-passing or write-ready), or blocked. Fail-closed and read-only like activation-result.py: any unmet condition is a named refusal, ambiguity is blocked rather than guessed, no input combination yields two states or none. The conductor owns classification: a finding classified blocking (acceptance-criteria violation, safety regression, corrupted evidence, failed authoritative gate) prevents completion; non-blocking findings become Seeds and a wave may complete with them. Workflow-process completion alone is never a product-success verdict.

title: Decide whether pstack can be onboarded, given it has no Claude Code front door
description: Operator asked 2026-08-19 whether pstack (github.com/cursor/plugins/tree/main/pstack, MIT, Lauren Tan) can join the closed external-library catalog alongside mattpocock/skills, ECC, and hyperresearch. Investigation found three obstacles, one currently fatal. (1) PROCESS: ADR-0009 2026-08-10 amendment closes the reachable catalog to exactly three rows and states a fourth is a new onboarding decision requiring licence, published-artifact front door, selection-surface cost, collision/ownership, credential, removal, docs, and executable-test evidence. Surmountable. (2) FATAL TODAY: pstack documents NO Claude Code front door. Its pristine README install section is exactly the Cursor slash command /add-plugin pstack; at HEAD the plugin manifest is .cursor-plugin/plugin.json in Cursor format and no .claude-plugin exists. library-front-doors.md requires citing a published artifact ("a README is a claim; the published artifact is the fact") and the installer warns a guessed flag is worse than a gap because a guess runs, so there is nothing legitimate to put in front_door or front_door_source. (3) SHAPE: pstack ships 44 skills plus 2 agents with ZERO name prefix, so name_prefix has no value and the collision precheck loses its only reinstall-versus-collision escape; as a plugin-channel install names would be namespaced, which reduces but does not remove the concern. Reopen when an upstream Claude Code distribution or .claude-plugin manifest exists to cite. Separately: a porting or generalization guide remains writable, but if it adapts pstack wording rather than pointing at it, ADR-0001 requires a root NOTICE donor entry in the same change citing the repo, commit, author, and MIT licence.

title: Gather pstack upstream evidence from pristine HEAD, never the ported working tree
description: CORRECTED 2026-08-19 after reading docs/progress/2026-08-19-pstack-claude-code-port.md. The original finding claimed the operator checkout misattributes four skills; that framing was wrong and is withdrawn. The port deliberately copied deslop, control-cli, and control-ui from the sibling cursor-team-kit because all three were already editor-agnostic, and authored create-skill from scratch because Cursor ships it as a built-in with no file implementation, so poteto-mode saying bundled with pstack is ACCURATE for the ported artifact. What survives is narrow and procedural: the tree at ~/.claude/local-plugins/pstack-src diverges from cursor/plugins@fd6dd6f by design (dirty by 5 untracked, 1 deleted, 39 modified, 12 renamed paths), so any future evidence about what UPSTREAM pstack ships - names, manifest shape, front door, licence surface - must be read from pristine git show HEAD and never from that working tree. Recorded so a later onboarding attempt does not cite the port as upstream.

title: Close the wave-journal residuals left by two review rounds
description: Non-blocking residuals from the agentic-sdlc-2b81 adversarial review and its blocker-fix round, none a merge blocker. TESTABILITY NOW AVAILABLE: _publish RENAME_NOREPLACE docstring still says it is the one guard no test kills because a test would need a forked racer, but the deterministic ordering seam added for the interleaving test makes init exposure drivable without timing - the paragraph is stale prose and the guard is now killable, so test it and correct the claim. VERDICT-TOOL GAP: nothing consumes journal_digest as the external head anchor that read_journal docstring names as the remedy for a rewritten last line or truncated tail; decide whether the verdict composer binds it. PERF, bounded: _unchanged_since_read adds a second full read per append, O(size) twice over an append-only file that only grows. DOC PRECISION: project_command deliberately discards the bound identity as a read-only verb, but the published journal_digest then describes the read rather than the file at the moment the caller acts on it - say so. RE-MEASUREMENT PIN: test_a_broken_stdout_really_costs_an_ordinary_process_its_exit_code pins measured CPython exit-1-versus-120 behaviour, so a Python pin bump reopens it. Plus six items from the first review round: docstring claims the code does not implement, _effect_ledger rationale citing a test that does not exist, the symlink test that passes on the kernel ELOOP strerror rather than the tool own classification, NoClockTests.PATTERNS missing time.time_ns/time.perf_counter/os.times where the stronger check is asserting the time module is never imported, the exit-code docstring overstating which codes each verb reaches, and approved-skip scope coverage if not already closed.

title: Close Implementation Decision 61: three wave outcomes are unimplemented
description: Found while building agentic-sdlc-bb44 and verified against the spec. Implementation Decision 61 (product spec lines 360-361) and user story 94 (line 164) close the wave-outcome set at SIX values: accepted, remediation-progress, blocked, aborted, failed, unknown-effect. Issue 07 Completion and adversarial review names only the first three, and wave-verdict.py implements those three. Slice 5 stated exit artifact is still satisfied because the map criterion names only an honest accepted or intended remediation-progress, but Decision 61 closure is NOT met. The builder reasoning for deferring, recorded as a residual in the emitted document, is sound and should be the starting point rather than re-litigated: aborted, failed, and unknown-effect describe how an execution ENDED rather than what its completion evidence shows, and no consumed artifact records them today, so such a wave currently reaches blocked with named reasons. Decide whether the wave journal gains lifecycle records for these three (making them derivable the way the other three are) or whether Decision 61 is re-scoped to separate execution outcome from completion verdict. Either answer needs the spec and issue 07 to agree afterwards.

title: Four wave-verdict input schemas are consumed but nothing produces them
description: Found while building agentic-sdlc-bb44. Four of the eight completion conditions had no emitting tool in this repository, so the composer defined and validates four input schemas itself: wave-artifact-manifest@1 (condition 3), wave-review-submission@1 (condition 4), wave-verdict-conductor-record@1 (condition 8), and wave-critic-findings@1 (the critic classification). All four are same-user assertions - validated for shape and cross-checked against the journal roles and sequence, never trusted on their own - but nothing in the bundle EMITS them, so the verdict currently depends on hand-authored evidence. Decide which producers are needed and where they live: the reviewer and critic roles plausibly emit two of them, the integrator or conductor the other two, and slice 6 planning and observability may own the conductor record. Until then a real wave cannot reach accepted without hand-written input, which is the honest limit of slice 5.

title: Wire wave-verdict into the flagship skill and fix the remediation-ready collision
description: Two documentation defects found while building agentic-sdlc-bb44. First: skills/agentic-sdlc/tools/wave-verdict.py is referenced by NO markdown in the bundle, because the ticket file set forbade touching existing files. It needs wiring into skills/agentic-sdlc/SKILL.md alongside the other tools, and the wave-journal and runtime-assignment tools from the same slice should be checked for the same gap. Second: issue 07 writes remediation-ready wave, but in the product spec remediation-ready is an ACTIVATION state (Decision 12, slice 4) while remediation-progress is the WAVE outcome (Decision 61, slice 5). Two different planes sharing a name invites exactly the conflation the verdict tool refuses, so correct issue 07 to say remediation-progress where it means the wave outcome. Per the prose-rot rule, run every command any edited sentence claims a result for.

title: pass-budget charge is not idempotent: a retry double-charges the ledger
description: Highest-harm finding from the agentic-sdlc-4253 exit-code enumeration, ranked first because it is the only one that actively corrupts state on retry rather than merely misreporting. skills/agentic-sdlc/tools/pass-budget.py charge increments the ledger with no idempotency guard, so a caller that retries after an ambiguous failure spends a second pass against both the phase and global budgets. Note the charge-then-check ordering at pass-budget.py:103 is DELIBERATE and correct - it exists so a crash cannot hand out free passes - so the fix is an idempotency key (attempt or operation id) that makes a repeated charge for the same attempt converge rather than accumulate, per the make-operations-idempotent discipline. The exit-code conformance work is the same ticket: a charge whose durable increment landed must not report a clean pre-effect refusal. Enumeration also corrected the umbrella premise: there are 24 CLI surfaces, not 8, of which 9 conform, 6 are read-only and effect-incapable so 3 and 4 are legitimately unreachable, and 8 are nonconforming; the prior 2-of-8 figure was an undercount. Full inventory with per-surface exit tables in .worktrees/artifacts/exit-code-conformance.md.

title: The conductor record seam cannot mutate blockedBy or blocks dependency edges
description: Real gap found behind stale bookkeeping by the legacy-seed reconciliation and confirmed live by the synthesis pass. The Seeds conductor-write seam admits only create and update over a records own fields; it cannot mutate blockedBy or blocks edges. All 18 edge-bearing records in the queue are legacy short-ids currently recommended for closure, so once those close the queue loses its dependency graph entirely and nothing can restore it through the admitted seam. Decide whether the seam gains an edge verb under the same compare-and-swap and exact-readback discipline, or whether dependency ordering moves into the slice-6 planning artifacts where WavePlan already carries edges. Do not close the 18 legacy records before this is settled, or the graph goes with them.

title: No unified pre-effect readiness guard exists or is queued
description: Real gap found by the legacy-seed reconciliation and confirmed by the synthesis pass: readiness checking is split across scripts/check-agentic-sdlc-prereqs.sh, the Seeds inspect ready and blocked verbs, and offline-inspect.py, which self-labels its result preview readiness only and explicitly disclaims Git-wave readiness. Legacy seed p3 covered part of this and is being recommended for closure as partly delivered, so the gap would otherwise disappear with it. Nothing provides one guard a caller can run before an effect to learn whether the whole set of required capabilities - Git, Seeds, trust, gates, selected adapter - is admitted, which is what the AGENTS.md fail-closed language assumes exists. Decide whether this is a new tool or a documented composition of the three existing surfaces, and note the honest constraint that a passing readiness check is evidence and never authorization.
